inheritanceRule: Every omitted field inherits the resolved parent class value.

profiles.name: Iron Tyrant

evidence.reason: Gauntlets, spiked gauntlets and armour spikes gain level-based weapon damage.

profiles.playerSummary: An armour-bound Antipaladin who turns gauntlets, armour spikes and a fiendish armour bond into his signature weapons and defence.
profiles.tradeoff: Touch of corruption, cruelties and the normal fiendish boon are replaced by a narrower armour-centred package.

profiles.name: White Mage

evidence.reason: Cleric cure spells, breath of life and group fast healing become dedicated class options.

profiles.playerSummary: An Arcanist who spends reservoir points and spell slots to deliver spontaneous cure magic, emergency revival and group fast healing.
profiles.tradeoff: Two general exploits are committed to healing, narrowing some of the Arcanist's modular freedom.

profiles.name: Titan Mauler

evidence.reason: High-level rage can enlarge the Barbarian at an increased rage cost.

profiles.playerSummary: A Barbarian specialised in oversized weapons and fighting creatures larger than herself, eventually growing during rage.
profiles.tradeoff: Several defensive and movement features are exchanged for a weapon style with unusual penalties and equipment needs.

profiles.name: Street Performer

professionIdentity.evidenceText: The archetype explicitly earns money performing and specialises in crowds, disguises and gathering street information.

evidence.reason: Several broad inspiration performances are replaced by concealment, self-protection and enemy disruption.

profiles.playerSummary: A streetwise Bard who hides allies, manipulates crowds, changes disguises quickly and humiliates enemies through performance.
profiles.tradeoff: Classic party-wide inspiration is reduced in favour of subterfuge and disruptive tricks.

profiles.name: Bloodrider

constraints.summary: The feral companion must be suitable for the Bloodrager to ride.

evidence.reason: A scaling rideable animal companion shares rage, resistances and personal spells.

profiles.playerSummary: A mounted Bloodrager bonded to a feral companion that shares parts of the character's bloodrage and bloodline magic.
profiles.tradeoff: The mount arrives at 5th level and replaces both forms of uncanny dodge.

profiles.name: Rageshaper

evidence.reason: Polymorph forms gain stronger natural attacks, faster movement and extended duration during bloodrage.

profiles.playerSummary: A Bloodrager who makes polymorph magic and bestial natural attacks a defining extension of bloodrage.
profiles.tradeoff: Blood sanctuary and improved uncanny dodge are lost for a specialised transformed-combat package.

profiles.name: Hinyasi

evidence.reason: Common improvised objects use unarmed-strike damage and become the archetype's supported weapons.
Improvised weapons deliver both damage and free combat manoeuvre attempts.

profiles.playerSummary: A Brawler who turns almost any nearby object into an effective weapon and uses it to trigger physical manoeuvres.
profiles.tradeoff: Shield proficiency, knockout and close-weapon mastery are exchanged for the improvised style.

profiles.name: Musketeer

constraints.summary: The gifted firearm cannot be sold, and its destruction suppresses the feature while a replacement is made.

evidence.reason: A scaling gifted firearm, reload support and focused full attacks replace mounted progression.
The standard Cavalier mount is explicitly replaced.

profiles.playerSummary: A Cavalier who gives up the mount to make an order-granted pistol or musket the focus of combat.
profiles.tradeoff: Mounted mobility and companion play disappear, while the character becomes highly dependent on one firearm.

profiles.name: Undead Lord

constraints.summary: The Death domain and Undead subdomain, when available, are mandatory and the second domain is lost.

evidence.reason: The Cleric creates and directly commands a persistent skeleton or zombie companion.
Domain choice is fixed and the second Cleric domain is lost.

profiles.playerSummary: A Cleric devoted to death magic with a persistent corpse companion and exceptional ability to command and restore undead.
profiles.tradeoff: Domain choice is tightly fixed and much of the specialised healing benefits undead rather than living allies.

profiles.name: Pack Lord

constraints.summary: An animal companion is mandatory and effective Druid levels must be permanently allocated among members of the pack.

evidence.reason: The normal companion progression is divided among a managed pack rather than increasing the already-core companion capability.

profiles.playerSummary: A Druid who divides normal companion progression among a personally managed pack and can perceive through its members.
profiles.tradeoff: Several weaker companions replace one full-strength companion, allocated levels are difficult to redistribute and a domain cannot be chosen.
